subject.title: fix(acp): close SQLite event ledger on shutdown to prevent file lock leaks

question: Should this ledger-level close API PR remain the landing candidate for the linked SQLite handle leak, or should maintainers switch to a shared-state shutdown close/drain fix?
rationale: Several open PRs target the same bug, and this branch adds a ledger lifecycle API plus a proof script while the current evidence points to the shared state DB close owner and an event-drain requirement.

options.title: Prefer shared close after drain
options.body: Use a fix that drains or invalidates in-flight ACP gateway handlers, then calls the shared state DB close owner once after final writes.

options.title: Repair this PR in place
options.body: Keep the ledger close API direction, but replace the direct open-and-close path, add event-handler drain coverage, remove the proof script, and require real behavior proof.

options.title: Pause duplicate candidates
options.body: Hold this PR and sibling candidates until one maintainer-approved shutdown lifecycle boundary is selected.

recommendation.title: Prefer shared close after drain
recommendation.body: Use a fix that drains or invalidates in-flight ACP gateway handlers, then calls the shared state DB close owner once after final writes.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent shared-state and ACP lifecycle history makes this the best available routing owner for the shutdown ownership decision.
